headline: Police find a stolen Picasso in a drug raid

sources.title: €12 Million Portrait of Picasso's 'Golden Muse' Recovered from Thieves After Paris Theft
A Stolen Picasso Just Turned Up During a Drug Raid Near Paris, Reportedly Taken From a Storage Facility
Picasso painting recovered in French drug raid was stolen 'opportunistically', police source says

chunks.text: French police {{carried out}} a [[raid]] on a house in Champigny-sur-Marne, near Paris. Officers went in to look for cannabis and cash, police said. Instead, they {{came across}} a [[stolen]] [[portrait]] by Pablo Picasso. Police said the painting is [[worth about]] 12 million euros. It shows Marie-Thérèse Walter, the artist's famous [[muse]].

verbs.correct: To do or perform a task or plan

verbs.wrong: To find something after a long search
verbs.correct: To find something by chance or by luck

chunks.text: The painting {{turned up}} next to [[bundles]] of cash, drugs, and expensive [[luxury]] goods, police said. Officers said the stolen artwork {{ended up}} in the house [[by chance]]. According to a police source, the thieves [[had no idea]] what to do with it. The house [[reportedly]] belonged to the aunt of a [[suspect]] in the drug case.

verbs.wrong: To be hidden in a very strange place
verbs.correct: To be found or to appear, often by chance

verbs.wrong: To be kept as a secret for years
verbs.correct: To finally be in a place or situation

chunks.text: Police said the theft was not [[carefully planned]]. One of the men worked as a security guard at a Paris [[warehouse]] where the portrait was kept before a sale. He {{made off with}} the painting, police said, but the [[gang]] could not {{get away with}} the crime [[for long]].

verbs.wrong: To hide something in a safe place
verbs.correct: To steal something and quickly leave

verbs.wrong: To hide from the police for a long time
verbs.correct: To do something wrong and not be punished for it

chunks.text: Police {{tracked down}} four men and [[arrested]] them, reports said. In court, one of them {{owned up to}} [[several]] thefts from the warehouse where he had worked. Officers {{took away}} the drugs, cash, and luxury goods as [[evidence]]. The [[valuable]] portrait will now be {{given back}} to its owner, police said.

verbs.wrong: To watch someone secretly for many days
verbs.correct: To find someone or something after searching hard

verbs.wrong: To give information about other criminals
verbs.correct: To admit that you did something wrong

verbs.wrong: To lock something in a safe place
verbs.correct: To remove something and carry it away

verbs.wrong: To put something back where it was found
verbs.correct: To return something to its owner

vocab.def: To do or perform a task or plan
ex: The police carried out a raid on the house early in the morning.
Doctors carried out several tests before the operation.
The team carried out the plan exactly as they had agreed.

vocab.def: To find something by chance or by luck
ex: During the raid, police came across a famous stolen painting.
I came across an old photo while cleaning my room.
He came across a rare coin at the market.

vocab.def: To be found or to appear, often by chance
ex: The missing painting turned up in a house near Paris.
My lost phone turned up under the sofa.
Old letters sometimes turn up in second-hand books.

vocab.def: To finally be in a place or situation
ex: The stolen artwork ended up in a drug dealer's house.
We got lost and ended up on the wrong side of town.
He ended up staying much longer than he had planned.

vocab.def: To steal something and quickly leave
ex: The guard made off with the painting while he was working.
Thieves made off with jewelry worth thousands of dollars.
Someone made off with my bike from outside the shop.

vocab.def: To do something wrong and not be punished for it
ex: The gang could not get away with the theft for long.
He thought he could get away with lying to his boss.
You will not get away with cheating on the test.

vocab.def: To find someone or something after searching hard
ex: Police tracked down four men and arrested them.
It took her years to track down her old friend.
The reporter tracked down the only witness to the crime.

vocab.def: To admit that you did something wrong
ex: In court, one man owned up to several thefts.
She owned up to breaking the window.
It takes courage to own up to your mistakes.

vocab.def: To remove something and carry it away
ex: Officers took away the drugs and cash as evidence.
The waiter took away our empty plates.
Please take away these boxes; they are in the way.

vocab.def: To return something to its owner
ex: The painting will be given back to its owner.
Can you give back the book I lent you last week?
He gave back the money he had borrowed.
My bike was stolen from outside the library.
The police found the stolen car in a parking lot.

wordDefs.def: Having a value of roughly a certain amount
ex: My old laptop is worth about 200 dollars.
That ring is worth about the same as my car.
I met my old teacher by chance at the market.
We found this little cafe by chance.
I had no idea the store closed so early.
She had no idea her friends were planning a party.

wordDefs.def: According to what people say or news reports
ex: The singer reportedly bought a house in the mountains.
The factory will reportedly close next year.

wordDefs.def: Prepared with a lot of thought and attention
ex: Their wedding was carefully planned for a whole year.
The trip was carefully planned down to the last day.

wordDefs.def: Used in negatives and questions to mean 'for a long time'
ex: I did not wait for long before the bus came.
He never stays angry for long.

wordDefs.def: Taken by the police because of a crime
ex: The driver was arrested after the accident.
Two men were arrested near the store last night.

wordDefs.def: More than two, but not many
ex: I called her several times yesterday.
We have several options for dinner.

wordDefs.def: Facts or objects that show something is true
ex: There was no evidence that he had lied.
The photos were used as evidence in court.
She keeps her valuable rings in a small box.
This old comic book is more valuable than it looks.

wordDefs.def: A sudden visit by police to search a place
ex: The raid began before sunrise.
Police made three raids that week.

wordDefs.def: A picture of a particular person
ex: The portrait hung in a back room.
He painted her portrait twice.

wordDefs.def: A person who inspires an artist
ex: She was his muse for ten years.
Every painter seems to have a muse.
Bundles of notes lay on the table.
He carried two bundles of paper.
Luxury watches filled the drawer.
They spent the money on luxury cars.

wordDefs.def: A person the police think may be guilty
ex: The suspect said nothing at first.
A second suspect was arrested later.

wordDefs.def: A large building where goods are stored
ex: The painting was kept in a warehouse.
He worked at the warehouse for a year.
The gang had four members.
Police followed the gang for months.

tf.s: Police made off with the stolen painting during the raid near Paris.
tf.why: Police came across and recovered the painting. Make off with means to steal something and quickly leave, which is not what the police did.

tf.s: In court, one man owned up to several thefts from the warehouse.
tf.why: The man owned up to the thefts, which means he admitted that he had done them.

tf.s: The stolen portrait turned up next to cash and drugs during the raid.
tf.why: The portrait turned up, which means it was found, next to the cash and drugs in the house.

tf.s: Police officers came across the stolen Picasso while searching the house.
tf.why: Police came across the painting, which means they found it by chance during the drug raid.

tf.s: The security guard gave back the painting while he worked at the warehouse.
tf.why: The guard made off with the painting, which means he stole it. Give back means to return something to its owner, the opposite of what he did.

tf.s: Police said the valuable Picasso will be taken away from its owner.
tf.why: Police said the painting will be given back to its owner, meaning returned to them. Take away means to remove something, the opposite of returning it.
